newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Petronas says optimistic on Vietnam Bear oilfield.
newsitem.headline: Petronas says optimistic on Vietnam Bear oilfield.

text.p: Malaysia's state oil company Petronas said on Wednesday it was optimistic about the prospects of a Vietnamese oilfield which Australia's Broken Hill Propriety Co Ltd has given up on.
"We feel we can better optimise the cost and therefore make it viable to operate the Bear Field," Petronas president Hassan Marican told reporters.
The Bear Field, or Dai Hung, was 43.75 percent owned by BHP until the company decided in February to divest its stake to Petronas, which originally owned 20 percent of the oilfield.

Hassan said he believed Petronas could also derive synergy and more efficiency from the oilfield as the Malaysian company was also producing oil from two blocks in the Ruby field, adjacent to the Dai Hung.
"Different operators have different operating philosophies, cost structures," he said. "In the case of Petronas, it was out presence in the Blocks 1 and 2 (of the Ruby field)."

Petronas' Ruby field in Block 01 and Block 02 has estimated reserves of 200 million barrels. Petronas says Ruby is expected to produce 9,500 barrels per day (bpd) by the year-end and 85,000 bpd by 2003.
Analysts have said Petronas has also made discoveries in the Topaz and Emerald fields, giving it the means to be a major long-term player in Vietnam's oil industry.
Although Petronas has decided to buy out BHP's stake, Hassan said the Vietnamese government had to still approve the deal.
"We're waiting for that approval now...we have taken the necessary steps," he said.
The Dai Hung, once thought of to be among Asia's biggest untapped oilfields, has been a big disappointment for BHP.
The oilfield was originally estimated to have had 700 million barrels of recoverable reserves but now that has been pared down to 100 million, experts said.
Output from the area has also fallen from 35,000 bpd to 12,000 bpd since production began in 1993.
Apart from Petronas, other partners in the venture are state-owned PetroVietnam, which has a 15 percent stake and Japan's Sumitomo Corp and France's Total SA, which have 10.625 percent each.
